findings.title: A rejected device is cached as successfully tagged
findings.body: The cache entry is written before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` checks the device limit. If that check returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the entry remains cached; the next request from the same device returns nil at line 84 without checking the store, so anonymous authentication succeeds. This lets a device denied by the configured limit bypass the limit for the cache lifetime. Only cache the device after a successful store operation, or remove the entry on error.

findings.title: The limit check and insert are not atomic
findings.body: Concurrent requests can each count fewer than `deviceLimit` rows, then both insert distinct devices. Because the count and insert run in separate database sessions with no locking or constraint enforcing the cap, the active-device total can exceed the configured limit under load. Enforce the check and insert atomically (or serialize limit checks across instances).
